ui.offline_intro: There is no network. I will guide you to collect what I need and give you a first opinion now. The full analysis comes when the network is back.
ui.survey_intro: I will guide you step by step. Do what I say, then press the big button.
ui.p_field: Step back and take a photo of the whole field.
ui.p_plant: Take a photo of one whole sick plant, from the soil to the top.
ui.p_leaf: Hold one sick leaf a hand's width from the camera, in good light, and take a photo.
ui.p_under: Turn that leaf over and take a photo of the underside.
ui.p_stem: Take a photo of the bottom of the stem, where it meets the soil.
ui.p_roots: Pull one sick plant out gently and take a photo of its roots.
ui.p_soil: Dig a hole as deep as your hand next to a sick plant and take a photo of the soil inside.
ui.q_pattern: Where in the field is the problem?
ui.q_pattern.0: A few plants here and there
ui.q_pattern.3: Along the edges or in low spots
ui.q_water: How does the crop get water?
ui.q_weather: How was the weather these past days?
ui.q_applied: What have you put on the crop recently?
ui.q_applied.2: A spray against pests or disease
ui.q_size.1: About a quarter of a hectare
ui.voice_note: If you want, press the button and tell me anything else about the problem. Press again when you finish.
ui.looks_like: From the photo, this looks like
ui.not_sure: I cannot tell from this photo alone.
ui.healthy: This leaf looks healthy to me.
ui.saved_wait: I have saved everything. When the network is back I will analyse it fully and prepare your plan.
ui.syncing: The network is back. I am analysing what you collected.

apple.scab.name: Apple scab
apple.scab.what: You see olive green to black velvety spots on the leaves, and dark rough scabby spots on the fruit.
now: Pick off the worst spotted leaves and fruit and burn them or bury them deep.
Prune out crowded branches so air and sun get inside the tree.
If it is spreading, spray a fungicide with captan or mancozeb in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
apple.scab.later: Rake up and destroy all fallen leaves in the fall, and plant scab resistant apple kinds when you can.

apple.black_rot.name: Apple black rot
apple.black_rot.what: The leaves get small purple spots that turn brown in the middle like a frog's eye, and the fruit rots black from the blossom end.
now: Cut off dead branches and sunken cankers, going well below the damage.
Pick off all rotten and dried up fruit, on the tree and on the ground, and destroy it.
If it keeps spreading, spray a fungicide with captan in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
apple.black_rot.later: Every winter, prune out dead wood and take down all dried up old fruit so the fungus has nowhere to wait.

apple.cedar_rust.name: Cedar apple rust
apple.cedar_rust.what: You see bright yellow orange spots on top of the leaves, often with little tubes or fringes underneath.
now: Look for cedar or juniper trees nearby and cut off the brown galls on them.
Pick off the worst spotted leaves and destroy them.
If many leaves are hit, spray a fungicide with myclobutanil in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
apple.cedar_rust.later: Take out nearby cedars or junipers if you can, and plant rust resistant apple kinds.

cherry.powdery_mildew.name: Cherry powdery mildew
cherry.powdery_mildew.what: You see white powder like flour on the young leaves, and the leaves curl up.
now: Cut off the worst covered shoots and destroy them.
Thin the tree out so air moves through it, and keep water off the leaves.
Spray a fungicide with sulfur in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
cherry.powdery_mildew.later: Prune every winter for an open tree, and start spraying early in spring before the white shows up.

maize.gray_leaf_spot.name: Gray leaf spot on corn
maize.gray_leaf_spot.what: You see long narrow gray to tan spots with straight edges running between the leaf veins, starting on the lower leaves.
now: Check how high up the leaves the spots have climbed, since spots near the ear leaf hurt the crop most.
Pull weeds and don't water from overhead, to keep the leaves dry.
If the spots are climbing fast before the tassels come out, spray a fungicide with azoxystrobin or propiconazole in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
maize.gray_leaf_spot.later: Don't plant corn after corn, plow under the old stalks, and pick a resistant seed.

maize.common_rust.name: Common rust on corn
maize.common_rust.what: You see small rusty brown raised bumps on both sides of the leaf that leave a brown powder on your fingers.
now: Check how much of the leaf is covered, since a few bumps don't hurt much.
Keep the crop well fed and watered so it stays strong.
If the bumps are thick on the upper leaves before tasseling, spray a fungicide with propiconazole or azoxystrobin in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
maize.common_rust.later: Plant a rust resistant corn seed and plant early in the season.

maize.northern_leaf_blight.name: Northern corn leaf blight
maize.northern_leaf_blight.what: You see long gray green to tan spots shaped like a cigar, as long as your finger or longer, starting on the lower leaves.
now: Watch how fast the spots move up the plant, especially in wet weather.
Pull weeds and space the plants out so the leaves dry quickly.
If it reaches the upper leaves before the silks, spray a fungicide with azoxystrobin or propiconazole in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
maize.northern_leaf_blight.later: Rotate to a crop that isn't corn, plow under old stalks, and plant a resistant seed.

grape.black_rot.name: Black rot on grapes
grape.black_rot.what: You see round brown spots with dark edges on the leaves, and the grapes shrivel into hard black raisins.
now: Pick off every shriveled black grape and spotted leaf and destroy them.
Thin the leaves around the bunches so the sun and air dry them out.
Spray a fungicide with mancozeb or myclobutanil in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
grape.black_rot.later: In winter, take every dried up grape off the vine and the ground, and start spraying when the new shoots come out.

grape.esca.name: Esca or black measles on grapes
grape.esca.what: The leaves get yellow or red stripes between the veins that turn brown like a tiger stripe, and the grapes get little dark spots.
now: Mark the sick vines so you can find them in winter.
Cut off dead arms well below the dark wood and burn them.
Clean your pruning tools with bleach water between vines, since no spray will cure this.
grape.esca.later: Prune in dry weather, cover big pruning cuts with wound sealer, and replace vines that keep dying.

grape.leaf_blight.name: Isariopsis leaf spot on grapes
grape.leaf_blight.what: You see dark brown spots with no clear edge on older leaves, and the leaves dry up and drop early.
now: Pick off the spotted leaves and destroy them.
Thin the vine so air moves through and the leaves dry fast.
If it keeps spreading, spray a fungicide with copper or mancozeb in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
grape.leaf_blight.later: Clean up fallen leaves after harvest and keep the vines open and pruned.

citrus.greening.name: Citrus greening
citrus.greening.what: The leaves get blotchy yellow patches that don't match on both sides, and the fruit stays small, lopsided, green, and bitter.
now: Mark the tree, because there is no cure, and a sick tree spreads it to the others.
Look on new shoots for tiny bugs called psyllids that sit at an angle with their tail up.
To kill the psyllids, spray an insecticide with imidacloprid in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
citrus.greening.later: Pull out and destroy sick trees, buy only certified clean young trees, and keep after the psyllids.

peach.bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial spot on peaches
peach.bacterial_spot.what: You see small dark angled spots on the leaves that fall out and leave holes, plus dark pitted spots on the fruit.
now: Cut off badly hit twigs and pick up fallen leaves.
Don't water from overhead, and don't work in the trees when they're wet.
Spray a copper product, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
peach.bacterial_spot.later: Plant resistant peach kinds, and spray copper at leaf drop and before buds open.

pepper.bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial spot on peppers
pepper.bacterial_spot.what: You see small dark wet looking spots on the leaves that turn brown, and the leaves turn yellow and drop.
now: Pull off the spotted leaves and badly hit plants and destroy them.
Water at the base of the plant and stay out of the patch when the leaves are wet.
Spray a copper product, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
pepper.bacterial_spot.later: Use clean seed or transplants, and don't grow peppers or tomatoes in that spot for two or three years.

potato.early_blight.name: Early blight on potatoes
potato.early_blight.what: You see brown spots with rings inside like a target on the lower leaves, with yellow around them.
now: Pull off the lower spotted leaves and destroy them.
Feed and water the plants well, since weak plants get hit hardest.
Spray a fungicide with chlorothalonil or mancozeb in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
potato.early_blight.later: Rotate away from potatoes and tomatoes for two or three years and clean up the old vines.

potato.late_blight.name: Late blight on potatoes
potato.late_blight.what: You see big dark wet looking patches on the leaves, with white fuzz underneath in damp weather, and it spreads very fast.
now: Pull up the sick plants right away, bag them or bury them deep, and don't compost them.
Hill dirt up over the potatoes so the spores can't reach them.
Spray the healthy plants with a fungicide with mancozeb or chlorothalonil in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
potato.late_blight.later: Plant certified clean seed potatoes, destroy volunteer potatoes and cull piles, and pick resistant kinds.

squash.powdery_mildew.name: Powdery mildew on squash
squash.powdery_mildew.what: You see white powder like flour on top of the leaves, starting with the older ones.
now: Pull off the worst covered leaves and throw them away.
Water at the base in the morning and give the plants room to breathe.
Spray a fungicide with sulfur in it, or potassium bicarbonate, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
squash.powdery_mildew.later: Plant mildew resistant squash kinds, and space them out with lots of sun.

strawberry.leaf_scorch.name: Leaf scorch on strawberries
strawberry.leaf_scorch.what: You see lots of small dark purple spots on the leaves that grow together until the leaf looks burned and dries up.
now: Pull off the spotted leaves and destroy them.
Water at the base early in the day and keep weeds down.
If it keeps spreading, spray a fungicide with captan in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
strawberry.leaf_scorch.later: Mow or clean up old leaves after harvest, and replant with clean plants every few years.

tomato.bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial spot on tomatoes
tomato.bacterial_spot.what: You see small dark greasy spots on the leaves and raised scabby spots on the green fruit.
now: Pull off spotted leaves and destroy them.
Water at the base and stay away from the plants when they're wet.
Spray a copper product, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
tomato.bacterial_spot.later: Use clean seed and transplants, and don't grow tomatoes or peppers there for two or three years.

tomato.early_blight.name: Early blight on tomatoes
tomato.early_blight.what: You see brown spots with rings inside like a target on the lower leaves, with yellow around them.
now: Pull off the lower spotted leaves and destroy them.
Put straw or mulch on the ground so dirt doesn't splash up on the leaves.
Spray a fungicide with chlorothalonil or mancozeb in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
tomato.early_blight.later: Rotate away from tomatoes and potatoes for two or three years and stake the plants up off the ground.

tomato.late_blight.name: Late blight on tomatoes
tomato.late_blight.what: You see big dark wet looking patches on the leaves and stems, and brown greasy blotches on the fruit, and it spreads very fast.
now: Pull out the sick plants right away, bag them or bury them deep, and don't compost them.
Keep the leaves dry and don't water from overhead.
Spray the healthy plants with a fungicide with chlorothalonil or mancozeb in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
tomato.late_blight.later: Plant resistant tomato kinds, and keep potato plants and cull piles away from your tomatoes.

tomato.leaf_mold.name: Leaf mold on tomatoes
tomato.leaf_mold.what: You see pale yellow patches on top of the leaves, with olive green to brown fuzz underneath.
now: Pull off the sick leaves and destroy them.
Open up the greenhouse or tunnel and prune the lower leaves so air can move.
If it keeps spreading, spray a fungicide with chlorothalonil or copper in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
tomato.leaf_mold.later: Keep the air moving and the humidity down, and plant leaf mold resistant kinds.

tomato.septoria.name: Septoria leaf spot on tomatoes
tomato.septoria.what: You see lots of small round spots with gray centers and dark edges on the lower leaves, often with tiny black dots inside.
now: Pull off the lower spotted leaves and destroy them.
Mulch the ground and water at the base.
Spray a fungicide with chlorothalonil or copper in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
tomato.septoria.later: Clean up all old tomato plants after harvest and rotate away from tomatoes for two or three years.

tomato.spider_mites.name: Spider mites on tomatoes
tomato.spider_mites.what: The leaves get tiny pale speckles and turn bronze, and you see fine webbing and tiny moving dots underneath.
now: Spray the underside of the leaves hard with water to knock the mites off.
Pull off the worst hit leaves and keep the plants well watered.
If they keep coming back, spray insecticidal soap, or a miticide with abamectin in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
tomato.spider_mites.later: Keep down dust and weeds, water well in hot dry spells, and don't overuse bug sprays that kill the good bugs that eat mites.

tomato.target_spot.name: Target spot on tomatoes
tomato.target_spot.what: You see brown spots with rings inside like a target, on the leaves, stems, and fruit.
now: Pull off the spotted leaves and destroy them.
Prune the lower leaves and space the plants so the air moves through.
Spray a fungicide with chlorothalonil or azoxystrobin in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
tomato.target_spot.later: Clean up old plants after harvest and rotate away from tomatoes.

tomato.yellow_leaf_curl.name: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus
tomato.yellow_leaf_curl.what: The top leaves stay small, curl up, and turn yellow at the edges, the plant stays stunted, and few fruit set.
now: Pull up the sick plants, bag them, and get rid of them, since there's no cure.
Check the underside of the leaves for tiny white flies that spread it.
To cut down the whiteflies, spray insecticidal soap, or an insecticide with imidacloprid in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
tomato.yellow_leaf_curl.later: Plant resistant tomato kinds, use clean transplants, and cover young plants with fine netting.

tomato.mosaic.name: Tomato mosaic virus
tomato.mosaic.what: The leaves get a mottled light and dark green pattern, sometimes curled or shaped like a fern, and the plant grows poorly.
now: Pull up the sick plants, bag them, and get rid of them, since there's no cure.
Wash your hands with soap and clean your tools before you touch healthy plants.
Don't smoke or handle tobacco around the plants, because it can carry the virus.
tomato.mosaic.later: Use certified clean seed and resistant kinds, and clean up all old plants after harvest.

rice.brown_spot.name: Brown spot on rice
rice.brown_spot.what: You see round to oval brown spots with gray centers on the leaves, and the grain can turn dark too.
now: Check the soil, since this shows up most in hungry, poor soil.
Give the crop a balanced fertilizer with potash in it.
If it's bad, spray a fungicide with propiconazole or mancozeb in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
rice.brown_spot.later: Use clean treated seed and build up the soil with balanced fertilizer and good water.

rice.leaf_blast.name: Rice blast
rice.leaf_blast.what: You see spots shaped like a diamond or an eye, with gray centers and brown edges, on the leaves.
now: Hold off on nitrogen fertilizer for now, because it makes blast worse.
Keep the field flooded evenly so it doesn't dry out.
If it's spreading, spray a fungicide with tricyclazole or azoxystrobin in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
rice.leaf_blast.later: Plant blast resistant rice, use clean seed, and split up your nitrogen into smaller amounts.

wheat.brown_rust.name: Leaf rust on wheat
wheat.brown_rust.what: You see small round orange brown bumps scattered on the leaves that rub off like rusty powder.
now: Check how much of the top leaves are covered.
Walk the field every few days to see how fast it moves.
If the flag leaf is getting covered, spray a fungicide with tebuconazole or propiconazole in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
wheat.brown_rust.later: Plant rust resistant wheat and get rid of volunteer wheat between seasons.

wheat.yellow_rust.name: Stripe rust on wheat
wheat.yellow_rust.what: You see yellow powdery bumps lined up in stripes along the leaves.
now: Look for the first patches in the field, since it spreads fast in cool wet weather.
Check the top leaves every few days.
If it's spreading, spray a fungicide with tebuconazole or propiconazole in it, follow the dose on the label, and cover your skin, mouth and eyes.
wheat.yellow_rust.later: Plant stripe rust resistant wheat and get rid of volunteer wheat between seasons.
